summary: The proposed @engramport/sdk slice is infeasible as written: its mandatory success criteria contradict its own bounds and the current tree. Claim 2 is not honestly coverable by a wrapper because Port Watch no longer has durable cursors (position is log-derived) while site copy still advertises them and bounds forbid site/protocol/envelope edits. Required out-of-prefix refusal is not in the supplied event-core and cannot be added without exceeding SDK-only bounds or decoupling from the required event-core mutation. The advertised package name plus an unchanged four-claim site repeats F112; a two-of-four product SDK is not progress under those bounds. Envelope-first is the coherent sequence. Observation disposition does not close ACTOR_UNREGISTERED. Named builder, executed= baseline, and several cited prior proofs are not in this packet.
findings: Claim 2 is not deliverable by this wrapper. Agent-a equates existing listInbox/work-delivery with the site sentence that Port Watch delivers work through durable cursors. packages/port-watch/src/index.mjs derives position from the log, migrates cursor/active_run/completions away, and rewind() throws POSITION_DERIVED_FROM_LOG. Bounds forbid site copy and protocol change, so the SDK cannot cover the advertised claim 2 contract. That is the F112 pattern, not a smaller honest slice.

The product name is what makes two-of-four dishonest. Wrapping appendEvent plus inbox discovery as an internal git-v0 client would be feasible. Declaring package.json name @engramport/sdk while app/page.tsx still lists safe retries, bounded context, and completion criteria, with no site copy change, occupies the architecture SDK slot with a partial client. Envelope-first is required if the SDK is meant to ship once: schema_version is hardcoded to 0 in event-core.mjs and retry/intent-digest/completion_criteria/bounded_context do not exist, so a public SDK API designed now is a v0 freeze or a breaking follow-up.

Required evidence fights the stated bounds. validateAppendInputs only scans credentials and path.resolve()s artifact paths; no artifact-prefix refusal is in the supplied event-core. Putting that control in event-core exceeds “SDK package, manifest, and workspace wiring.” Putting it only in the SDK means an event-core mutation would not break that refusal, so the coupling evidence and the prefix evidence cannot both hold. “Never-overwrite proven structurally” is already inherited from append-to-events/<actor> with wx; restating it does not create a new SDK property.

Work-delivery is not a thin SDK facade. PortWatch requires an AUTHORIZED inbox source, file-backed control store, git exec for log state, and FileClaimStore leases. Exporting that path as @engramport/sdk either leaks supervisor control-plane into a client library or silently ships only listInboxEntries while claiming Port Watch delivery. gitAuthorizedInboxSource must remain the only inbox query; an SDK-level unauthorized loader would be a security-boundary gap.

Observation disposition being durable and session_user-bound does not give git-v0 a coherent ACTOR_UNREGISTERED story. Enrollment in Postgres and actors/*.yaml remain different identity planes. An SDK over event-core still takes a free-form actor string and writes under events/<actor>/; the Postgres control stream cannot authorize that append. Treat ACTOR_UNREGISTERED as unchanged.

Agent-a’s framing hid missing prerequisites and unverified prior claims. The proposed dispatch names no builder, so strict_relay has no actor with authority to edit shared packages/ and root package.json (which has no workspaces field today). Completion depends on executed= moving from a value “agent-b states” that is not in this packet. GIT_ADAPTER_CORE_DELEGATION, duplicate-invocation discrimination, observation.mjs, and executed=140 are not in the supplied files; they cannot be treated as closed. “Repository log verifies against an SDK-produced event” is also ill-posed: a real append mixes a package proof into the collaboration log; a test fixture is not the repository log. Do not send this dispatch. Rename and narrow to append+inbox without product branding, or dispatch the settled envelope/retry slice first and then one complete SDK.
